title: (a) little (a) few
subtitle: a little water / a few books
summary: Use (a) little with uncountable nouns and (a) few with plural nouns, and remember that a little/a few is a positive idea but little/few is a negative one.

lesson.heading: a little = some but not much

left.label: a little
examples: She didn't eat anything, but she drank **a little water**.
I speak **a little Spanish**. (= some Spanish but not much)

right.label: a few
examples: Excuse me, I have to make **a few phone calls**.
We're going away for **a few days**.
*A:* Are there any shops near here? *B:* Yes, **a few**.

lesson.heading: little and few without a
lesson.text: **little** (without *a*) = nearly no or nearly nothing. **few** (without *a*) = nearly no. You can also say **very little** and **very few**.

examples.text: There was **little food** in the fridge. It was nearly empty.
There were **few people** in the theatre. It was nearly empty.
Dan is very thin because he eats **very little**. (= nearly nothing)
Your English is very good. You make **very few mistakes**.

left.label: a little / a few = positive
left.text: The speaker is happy: they have got some.
examples: They have **a little** money, so they're not poor. (= they have some money)
I've got **a few** friends, so I'm not lonely. (= I've got some friends)

right.label: little / few = negative
right.text: The speaker is not happy: they have got nearly none.
examples: They have **little** money. They are very poor. (= nearly no money)
I'm sad and I'm lonely. I've got **few** friends. (= nearly no friends)

lesson.text: *I've got **a little** money* is good news. *I've got **little** money* is bad news. The small word **a** changes everything.

exercises.explanation: money is uncountable, so a little.
envelopes is a plural noun, so a few.

exercises.prompt: Does each noun go after a little or after a few?
Can I have ___ in my coffee, please?
exercises.explanation: milk is uncountable, so a little milk.

exercises.prompt: Martin speaks Italian well. He lived in Italy for ___ .
exercises.explanation: years is plural, so a few years.

exercises.prompt: Your English is very good. You make ___ .
exercises.explanation: very few = nearly no; mistakes is a plural noun.

exercises.prompt: The weather here is very dry in summer. There is ___ .
exercises.explanation: very little = nearly none; rain is uncountable.

exercises.prompt: There was ___ food in the fridge. It was nearly empty.
exercises.explanation: little (without a) = nearly nothing, and food is uncountable.

exercises.prompt: 'When did Sarah go out?' '___ minutes ago.'
exercises.explanation: minutes is plural and the meaning is positive, so A few.
Everybody needs a little luck. Here the meaning is positive, so we need a.

exercises.statement: Martin is a very private person. Few people know him well.
exercises.explanation: Correct: few people = nearly no people, a negative idea.

exercises.prompt: You will be away for three days. Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: We're going away for a few days next week.
exercises.explanation: days is plural, so we say for a few days.
